title: Open a unit through its key concept
statement: In a course's first lesson, call up prior knowledge through the unit's key concept, such as a word web hinting at last year's text, not straight retrieval from it.
example: A Grade 9 first lesson that tried retrieval from a play studied in Grade 8 found it confusing and opened with a word web on the unit's key concept instead.
detail: At a planning meeting on 1 October 2026, a draft first lesson for a Grade 9 unit was described: retrieval from a play the learners read the year before had come across as confusing, so the lesson put the unit's key concept, deceit, on screen for a word web, with a hint asking what words would describe a character from that earlier play, so that the unit's words link back to it (`g9/sources/meeting-notes/ELA - CNU + Academics - 2026_10_01 20_30 IST - Notes by Gemini.md`, line 272). The later video sheet hands over to that word web as the first lesson's retrieval (`g9/sources/Othello Unit Video_ Info Sheet for Devfactory.md`, line 48).
against: It is one lesson draft's choice, untested with learners.

evidence.path: sources/meeting-notes/ELA - CNU + Academics - 2026_10_01 20_30 IST - Notes by Gemini.md
evidence.quote: I kind of played with the idea of putting McBTH retrieval because they will have done McBTH in grade eight but it was coming across quite confusing.

evidence.path: sources/meeting-notes/ELA - CNU + Academics - 2026_10_01 20_30 IST - Notes by Gemini.md
evidence.quote: So what I've done because it's the first unit is put the word deceit up and I want them to create a word web around that word and then there's a hint there of like what kind of words would you use to describe Lady McBth.
